My partner and I had arranged for her mum to take our two-year-old for the weekend. On Saturday afternoon I took LSD, about 120ug, while my partner went to a friend's birthday. I thought I had the house to myself until the evening. Around two hours in, my partner called. Her mother had fallen and broken her wrist, my partner was taking her to A&E, and our daughter was in the car with them and would be dropped off at home in ten minutes because she couldn't sit in a hospital for hours. My partner didn't know I'd taken anything.

I said 'okay' because I didn't know what else to say. I tried to sober up, splashing water on my face, which of course does nothing. When the doorbell rang, my partner handed me our daughter and left in a hurry. And then I was alone with a toddler while tripping hard.

She wanted to play. She wanted dinner. She wanted her bath. Everything she asked for was a mountain. Her face kept changing, sometimes she looked like a baby, sometimes like an old woman, sometimes her eyes were huge and black. I was terrified that I'd drop her, that I'd hurt her, that I'd forget she was there. I kept counting her fingers. When she cried because I couldn't find her favourite cup, the crying filled the whole house and the walls pulsed with it. I felt like the worst father in the world and that this was a test I was failing.

I sat on the floor of her room with her on my lap for hours, reading the same book over and over because it was the only thing I could manage. The words on the page kept moving. I didn't dare give her a bath. I gave her bread and a banana for dinner. She fell asleep on me around 9pm, and I didn't move until my partner came home at midnight. I told her I had a migraine.

Ich war bei einem Ayahuasca-Retreat in Portugal. In der zweiten Nacht ist ein anderer Teilnehmer, ein großer Mann, plötzlich aufgesprungen und hat angefangen zu schreien, dass wir alle Dämonen sind. Die Helfer haben versucht, ihn zu beruhigen, aber er hat sie weggestoßen. Dann ist er auf mich losgegangen, weil ich ihm am nächsten lag. Er hat mich an den Schultern gepackt, geschüttelt und mir ins Gesicht geschrien. Ich war mitten in meinen eigenen Visionen und sah sein Gesicht als Fratze mit Hörnern. Ich dachte, ich werde jetzt getötet. Zwei Helfer haben ihn schließlich weggezogen und nach draußen gebracht. Ich lag den Rest der Nacht zitternd auf meiner Matte, unfähig mich zu bewegen, und jedes Geräusch von draußen hat mich zusammenzucken lassen. Ich hatte das Gefühl, dass er zurückkommt. Am nächsten Morgen war er weg, und die Leitung hat kaum darüber gesprochen.

My friends dared me to take mushrooms in the old cemetery at night. I thought it'd be a laugh. I started seeing figures standing between the graves, very still, watching. I was sure they were the dead and that they were angry we were there. I ran and fell over a gravestone and cut my knee. My friends thought it was funny until they saw how scared I was.

This is the first time I've written this down.

I was married to a man who was controlling and sometimes violent. I didn't see it that way at the time, I thought it was normal, that he was stressed, that I provoked him. He had done mushrooms when he was younger and kept saying they would 'open me up' and make me less uptight. I didn't want to, but he insisted, and saying no to him was never easy. So one Saturday when our kids were at his parents', we both took mushrooms.

For the first hour, I felt strangely clear. It was like a fog lifted. I looked at him and saw him, really saw him. I saw the coldness in his eyes. I saw all the times he'd hurt me, one after another, like slides. I'd been telling myself stories for nine years, and the mushrooms took the stories away.

He noticed I was looking at him differently and asked what was wrong. I said something, I don't remember exactly, something like 'you scare me'. That set him off. He started shouting that I was ungrateful, that I was crazy, that I was ruining the trip. He got very close to my face. On the mushrooms his face became huge and red and his voice boomed like thunder. Then he grabbed my arm and pulled me off the sofa and pushed me against the wall. My head hit the wall. I saw stars, real stars and mushroom stars together.

I don't know how I knew what to do, but I did. I went completely limp and quiet, because I knew from experience that if I fought, it would be worse. He let go and went to the kitchen to get a beer, still shouting. I sat on the floor, and in that state I had a single, very clear thought: if I stay, one day he'll kill me. It wasn't a hallucination. It was the clearest thought I'd ever had.

The rest of the trip was a nightmare. He calmed down after an hour and wanted to cuddle and 'have a nice trip', as if nothing had happened. I let him, because I was afraid. Inside, I felt my whole self cracking apart. I felt like I was two people, one lying on the sofa smiling, and one floating above, screaming. The walls were breathing, and I kept seeing the faces of my children. I lay there for hours, pretending, while my mind was howling.

Two weeks later, while he was at work, I took the kids and went to a women's shelter.

Ich hatte auf LSD ein Ego-Tod-Erlebnis. Am Anfang war das sehr angsteinflößend, ich dachte, ich verliere den Verstand und sterbe. Ich habe mich verzweifelt an meinem Namen festgehalten, und er ist mir trotzdem entglitten. Dann habe ich losgelassen, und es kam ein Gefühl von großer Weite und Frieden. Danach war ich sehr erschöpft, aber auch dankbar. Es war die schwierigste und gleichzeitig die wertvollste Erfahrung meines Lebens.

I was at a friend's house and he offered me DMT from a vape pen. I had smoked DMT once before and it was fine. What I didn't know was that this pen contained 5-MeO-DMT, which is a completely different substance and much stronger. I took one deep hit.

Instantly, everything disappeared. Not into visions, just into white nothingness. There was no me, no room, no world. I don't know how to describe it except as total annihilation. In that state there was no fear, because there was no one to be afraid.

The fear came when I started coming back. I was on the floor, I didn't know how. My body was doing things on its own, my arms and legs were jerking and I was making strange noises. I couldn't breathe properly. It felt like my chest had forgotten how. My friend told me later that I had stopped breathing for maybe 20 or 30 seconds and that he started shaking me and was about to call an ambulance when I gasped.

For the next 20 minutes I was in total terror. I didn't know who I was. I knew there had been nothing and that the nothing was still right there, behind everything, and that I could fall back into it any second. I clutched my friend's arm and kept asking him if I was alive. He was pale and scared. He kept apologising. I lay on his sofa for an hour, unable to stand, and every time I closed my eyes I felt the white nothing pulling at me.
LSD at a concert. I became convinced that the band was singing about me, that every lyric was a message about my life and my sins. Cried through the whole set.

Ich war im Erasmus-Semester in Spanien. An einem Wochenende bin ich mit ein paar Leuten aus dem Studentenwohnheim an die Küste gefahren, und wir haben am Strand LSD genommen. Es war meine erste Erfahrung. Am Anfang war es wunderschön, das Meer, die Sterne, das Lagerfeuer.

Irgendwann bin ich allein am Strand entlanggelaufen, weil ich das Meer sehen wollte. Ich habe mich verlaufen. Ich wusste nicht mehr, wo die anderen waren. Ich habe mein Handy aus der Tasche genommen, um sie anzurufen, und es ist mir in den Sand gefallen. Ich habe es nicht wiedergefunden. Ich hatte keine Ahnung, wie unser Hostel hieß, ich hatte nur die Adresse im Handy.

Es war Nacht, und ich war allein an einem fremden Strand in einem fremden Land und konnte kaum Spanisch. Drei Männer kamen auf mich zu und haben mich angesprochen. Ich habe nicht verstanden, was sie wollten. Einer hat mich am Arm gefasst, ein anderer hat gelacht. Ich habe mich losgerissen und bin weggerannt, barfuß, durch den Sand und dann über eine Straße. Ich weiß nicht, ob sie mir gefolgt sind. In meinem Kopf waren sie überall, hinter jedem Auto, in jedem Schatten.

Ich habe mich hinter einen Müllcontainer gesetzt und bin bis zum Morgengrauen dort geblieben. Die Lichter der Straßenlaternen haben sich zu Augen verwandelt, die mich anstarren. Ich habe gebetet, dass es aufhört. Am Morgen hat mich eine ältere Frau gefunden, die ihren Hund ausgeführt hat. Sie hat mich mit in ihr Café genommen, mir einen Kaffee gegeben und mit ihrem Handy meine Mitbewohnerin über Facebook gesucht. Ich bin ihr unendlich dankbar.

I went to a jungle ceremony that I later learned was run by someone with a bad reputation. I drank the ayahuasca and within an hour I knew it was different from the brew I'd had before. My mouth was bone dry, my vision went blurry, and I couldn't pee. I started to see people who weren't there, ordinary people, a woman sweeping, a child in the corner, and I talked to them. I later found out the brew had toé in it, a datura species, which causes delirium. I don't remember large parts of the next two days. I remember waking up in a hammock with my hands tied, because apparently I'd been wandering into the jungle. I remember not knowing what country I was in. I remember a man holding a cup to my lips. The other participants said I was talking to invisible people for hours and tried to walk into the river.
Mushrooms. Nothing crazy happened, I just felt total dread for 5 hours for no reason.

Wir waren auf einer Bergtour in den Dolomiten und hatten beschlossen, am Gipfel eine kleine Dosis LSD zu nehmen. Die Dosis war wohl doch nicht so klein. Auf dem Rückweg mussten wir einen schmalen Grat überqueren, mit Abgründen auf beiden Seiten. Plötzlich hat sich der Grat bewegt, oder ich hatte das Gefühl, dass er sich bewegt. Die Tiefe hat mich angezogen, als würde sie mich rufen. Ich hatte Angst zu fallen und gleichzeitig Angst, dass ich springen will. Ich bin auf allen vieren weitergekrochen, zitternd und weinend. Meine Freunde mussten mich an der Hand nehmen und Schritt für Schritt führen. Es hat über eine Stunde gedauert, ein Stück, das man normalerweise in zehn Minuten geht. Ich war mir sicher, dass ich da oben sterbe. Als wir endlich auf sicherem Boden waren, bin ich zusammengebrochen.

I did a 'hippie flip' (mushrooms then MDMA) at a friend's flat. It went fine until my friends thought it'd be funny to tell me I'd been tripping for three days and that they'd been taking care of me. I believed them completely. I thought I'd lost three days of my life and that my brain was broken. I panicked, cried, tried to call my parents. They told me it was a joke an hour later but I couldn't shake the feeling.
